title: "Why Did You Lie?": Air India Crew Member Surprises Parents Onboard
excerpt: Sushmita Nath told her parents she was on a different flight — then waited at the aircraft door. Her mother's first words, "Juth kyu boli?" (Why did you lie?), melted millions of hearts.
body:
• Air India flight attendant Sushmita Nath surprised her parents by telling them she was operating a different flight — then waiting at the aircraft door to welcome them onboard.
  • Her father's first reaction was delight; her mother immediately asked, "Juth kyu boli?" (Why did you lie?), before the pride set in.
  • Nath said the minutes waiting for her parents were "the longest few minutes" of her day, and that the pride in their eyes was one of the most rewarding experiences of her career.
  • The video has drawn millions of views and emotional reactions from viewers, many writing about their own dreams of making their parents proud.

Air India flight attendant Sushmita Nath told a small lie at home — and turned it into a moment her parents will never forget. Nath informed her parents she had been rostered on a different flight, not the one they were travelling on. Instead, she stood waiting at the aircraft door, watching the entrance, as their flight began boarding.

She later described those minutes of waiting as the longest few of her day, spent in eager anticipation of their reaction. Her father walked in first, and she called out, "Papa." Moments later, her mother boarded, took in the scene — and asked the question that gave the viral video its title: "Juth kyu boli?" Why did you lie? Surprise quickly gave way to something warmer, as Nath said seeing the pride in her parents' eyes was one of the most rewarding experiences of her life.

Context & Background

Nath shared the video on her Instagram account, @sushmita__nath_, where it took off far beyond her own followers. Curly Tales reported that within just a few hours the clip had captured the attention of millions of people, and it has continued to circulate widely — including a new wave of attention this week after NDTV picked up the story.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=84nWEs75QxQ

Surprise-family videos have become a staple of Indian social media, but aviation ones carry a particular charge. For many Indian families, a child in an airline uniform represents years of competitive exams, training, and grooming — a hard-won professional milestone. Watching parents discover that milestone mid-boarding, in uniform, at the aircraft door, compresses the whole journey into a single frame.

Impact & Analysis

The comment section under Nath's video reads like a collective confession. "Oohh God, why do I have tears in my eyes?" wrote one viewer. "Amazing. Proud parents and a proud daughter. Keep shining," wrote another. One of the most-liked responses came from a viewer who admitted a similar dream remained unfulfilled: "I, too, had a similar dream of making my parents proud, but unfortunately, it hasn't been fulfilled yet. However, watching your video has rekindled hope within me."

The clip belongs to a small but potent genre of airline-family surprises that reliably goes viral: IndiGo captain Gurdish Singh's mid-flight shout-out to his daughter travelling on a school trip, a pilot flying his parents home as a surprise, and cabin crew orchestrating birthday celebrations at 36,000 feet. What distinguishes Nath's video is the deception — the tiny, loving lie that makes the reveal land harder. The mother's first response, an instinctive "why did you lie," only to melt seconds later, is what made the moment feel real rather than staged.

Diaspora Angle

The video has resonated deeply with Indian families abroad, where the distance from home makes such reunions rarer and sweeter. For diaspora parents whose children grew up outside India, seeing an Indian airline uniform worn with pride carries an added layer — proof that success can circle back to roots. And for the many NRIs who fly Air India regularly, the clip is a reminder that behind every uniform is a family story, and occasionally, a very good secret.

What's Next

Nath's video continues to rack up views and reactions, joining the long shelf of feel-good aviation moments that outlast any news cycle. For Air India, in the middle of a fleet and service transformation under the Tata group, a crew member's genuine moment of joy has done more for the brand's warmth than any campaign could. And for viewers still chasing their own version of the moment, one comment summed up the takeaway: keep going — the surprise, when it comes, is worth the wait.
nri_angle: The video resonates strongly with diaspora families, for whom reunions are rarer and an Air India uniform represents success that circles back to Indian roots.
